chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim al-Sayqal who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: A parchment was found in the handle of the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and in it was:

In the name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. The most insolent of people toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection is the one who kills someone other than his (intended) killer, and the one who strikes someone other than the one who struck him, and whoever befriends other than his (rightful) guardians — he is a disbeliever in what Allah revealed to Muhammad. And whoever initiates an offense or shelters an initiator, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any exchange nor any ransom.
He said: Then he (the Imam) said to me: 'Do you know what is meant by the one who befriends other than his guardians?' I said: 'What does it mean?' He said: 'It means the people of the Religion.'
And 'the exchange' is repentance according to the words of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and 'the ransom' is the sacrifice according to the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أعتى: The most insolent, arrogant, defiant — superlative of عتو (ʿutuww), meaning extreme arrogance and rebelliousness toward God
key_terms.الفداء: Sacrifice, ransom — redemptive payment or act of self-sacrifice
key_terms.ذؤابة: The handle/pommel or hanging strap at the hilt of a sword; here the place where the parchment was kept
key_terms.صرف: Exchange, repentance — a technical Quranic term (2:48, 2:123) meaning any form of compensation or repentance that might avert punishment
key_terms.عدل: Ransom, equivalent, compensation — another Quranic term for a substitute or ransom payment
key_terms.موالي: Guardians, patrons, loyal companions — in Shia theology specifically the Imams and their followers

ai.seo_question: What does the parchment found in the Prophet's sword say about retaliation and loyalty in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits the contents of a parchment found in the sword of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), containing three grave prohibitions: retaliating against someone other than one's actual assailant, taking unauthorized loyalty away from one's rightful guardians (understood here as the Imams and the people of the true Religion), and committing or sheltering criminal offenses. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains the Quranic term 'the one who befriends other than his guardians' as specifically referring to the people of the true Religion (i.e., the Shia faithful following the Imams). The two technical Quranic terms for divine acceptance — 'sarf' (exchange/repentance) and ''adl' (ransom/compensation) — are glossed by the Imams: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) identifies 'sarf' as repentance, while Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) identifies ''adl' as sacrifice. The early Muslim audience would have understood these terms as theological markers for the impossibility of divine intercession for such grave violations on the Day of Judgment.
